questions.q: In "Cost it: power, labour and trays Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Price by weight, and show what the buyer saves compared with what they pay now, in dollars per week.

Track yield per tray and days to harvest for every cycle so that you can compare runs.

questions.q: In "Run clean, steady operations Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Ask each for weekly volume, price they pay now and the freshness gap you can close.
Check the funding programmes' rules and dates yourself; do not assume a grant will arrive.
Test a 10% rise in power price and a 15% yield drop, and show the new margin and break-even for each.

questions.q: In "Sell, deliver and keep the customer Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Scout for pests and mould twice a week and remove problem trays at once.

Write an energy plan: efficient lamps, off-peak operating hours, and renewable power by contract or on the roof where allowed.

questions.q: In "Manage food safety and power risks Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?

Insurance for crop loss, equipment and liability should be arranged before the first harvest.
